sources.entry: phpBB - Flat-forum bulletin board software solution that can be used to stay in touch with a group of people or can power your entire website. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 PHP

summary.one_liner: phpBB is a free, open-source bulletin board (forum) software written in PHP.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes phpBB as a free open-source bulletin board written in PHP. It points users to phpBB.com for downloading the software and for community support. For developers, it explains how to clone the repository and install PHP dependencies with Composer to run a development build on a local server. It also links to Vagrant and GitHub Codespaces setups and to developer documentation covering core development, extensions, and automated testing. The README mentions unit and functional tests, with branches for master and 3.3.x.
use_cases: run a discussion forum for a group
power a community website with message boards
set up a local phpBB development environment
how_to_run: Fork phpbb/phpbb on GitHub and clone your fork locally
Alternatively, use the Vagrant or GitHub Codespaces setup described in the documentation
notable: Can run a simple forum or power an entire website, per the awesome-selfhosted listing
Development docs cover core, extensions, and automated testing
Supports Vagrant and GitHub Codespaces development setups
caveats: The README does not describe installation for end users beyond pointing to phpBB.com for pre-built packages
Contribution workflow requires a phpBB.com account and tickets
Automated test status badges are not shown in the README
keywords: run a forum for my group
stay in touch with a group
